groundTruth.note: What was planted. The engine has never seen this file — it is here so a reader can check the verdicts against the truth.
groundTruth.snrKnobNote: The generator input: how much of the forward return each cohort "sees" when it picks. NOT a target in bps.
groundTruth.realizedNote: The excess the generator actually produced at 48h, measured the same way the engine measures it. This is the column to compare verdicts against.
groundTruth.expectationDerivedFrom: realizedExcessBps48h, with an approximate significance threshold of 3 x 14 bps block-bootstrap SE = 42 bps

expectation.Fund: economic below roughly 81 bps of round-trip cost and fail-economic above it — realized excess 81.3 bps clears the bar, so the verdict turns on cost alone
expectation.Smart Trader: fail-signal at every cost — realized excess 1.4 bps is indistinguishable from drift
expectation.30D Smart Trader: fail-signal at every cost — realized excess 16.6 bps is REAL but below what a Bonferroni bar over 18 hypotheses can certify (~42 bps here). Correctly refused, not missed.
expectation.90D Smart Trader: fail-signal at every cost — realized excess 0.8 bps is indistinguishable from drift
expectation.180D Smart Trader: fail-signal at every cost — realized excess 6.7 bps is indistinguishable from drift
expectation.Smart HL Perps Trader: economic below roughly 160 bps of round-trip cost and fail-economic above it — realized excess 160 bps clears the bar, so the verdict turns on cost alone

groundTruth.theTestThatMatters: A cohort whose realized excess clears the bar must move between `economic` and `fail-economic` as cost crosses that excess, and must never fall to `fail-signal` on the way. A signal is real or it is not; cost cannot make it unreal. If any cohort crosses from economic straight to fail-signal as cost rises, the two verdicts have collapsed into one and the engine is broken.
